演奏者採坐姿，將馬達爾鼓橫置於身前，以雙手同時敲擊兩端鼓面。初學可先調整皮帶或繩: The player sits with the madal laid across the front of the body and strikes both heads at once with both hands. A beginner can first adjust the tightness of the straps or cords so that the tension of the heads is steady, then practise controlling the striking position and force so that the rhythm is clear. The sound is mainly made by striking the head with the palm, and attention should be paid to balancing the timbre of the two drums.
馬達爾由兩面大小不同的木製鼓組成，傳統以山羊或水牛皮為鼓面，以擊打鼓面發聲。較大: The madal is made of two wooden drums of different sizes, traditionally with goatskin or buffalo-hide heads, sounded by striking the head. The larger male drum has a deeper resonance and sounds higher, the smaller female drum lower; struck together they produce complex melody and rhythm. A thin skin gives a brighter, sharper timbre, a thick one a deeper sound, and the thickness and character of the wooden body and its resonance also affect the overall timbre. The tension of the straps or cords can tune the pitch. Like the modern drum it is a membranophone, but its two-drum structure gives a range from a crisp high to a deep low. 馬達爾鼓主要用於尼泊爾民間音樂的節奏支撐，也見於古典、宗教音樂與現代融合編制。它: The madal is used mainly to carry the rhythm in Nepali folk music, and also appears in classical and religious music and in modern fusion line-ups. It is usually played as a hand drum, laid across the body in a sitting position with both heads sounding at once. In Bollywood music, Ranjit Gazmer used it when working with Rahul Dev Burman, on pieces including 《Hum Dono Do Premi》 and 《Kanchi Re Kanchi Re》.
馬達爾鼓在尼泊爾有可追溯至古代的歷史，長期作為傳統音樂與文化慶典的重要打擊樂器，: The madal has a history in Nepal that goes back to ancient times; it has long been an important percussion instrument of traditional music and cultural celebration, and stands for Nepali identity and tradition. In the early twentieth century its form and function were much the same, and it remained at the centre of Nepali musical culture. Working with Rahul Dev Burman, Ranjit Gazmer brought the drum into Bollywood music, on songs such as Hum Dono Do Premi and Kanchi Re Kanchi Re; some Adivasi groups also use it.

馬達爾鼓（Madal）是尼泊爾傳統手鼓，屬膜鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sac: The madal is a traditional Nepali hand drum, a membranophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 211.232. The body is cylindrical and slightly bulging in the middle, with a skin at each end, one large and one small; it is usually laid across the body in a sitting position and both heads are struck at once. It is used mainly to carry the rhythm in Nepali folk music, and also appears in classical and religious music and in the playing of some Adivasi groups; it is the national instrument of Nepal.
